title: Autokey with skipped key positions
question: Does the complete source autokey-with-skips grid produce a full-page candidate above its English-score gate?
reader_question: Can recovered or encrypted runes continue a key when positions may be skipped?
summary: No candidate crossed the source English-score threshold in 9,900 full-page decodes. The source encoder and decoder follow different future-key rules in 247 of 360 known-message tests, limiting the result.
reader_finding: None of the 9,900 full-page outputs passed the English-score gate. But 247 of 360 known-message tests used different rules in the source encoder and decoder, so this does not rule out autokey.
reader_limit: All 113 valid known-message cases recovered exactly. Scores also accepted wrong text. Only these starting keys and source rules were tested; discarded beam paths and other autokey mechanisms remain outside the result.
finding: The complete 45-primer x two-model x two-sign x 55-segment source grid returns zero strict > -5.5 hits. Best -6.627310296014692: LOSS, ciphertext autokey, sign -1, LP2-49. Separately normalizing 2,099,107 retained terminal hypotheses improves 5,564 case scores but gives zero crossings; best normalized -6.519887696602062. Controls: P 54/180 and C 59/180 have an admissible complete true path and all 113 recover exactly. All 247 infeasible cases make future-key queries handled differently by the source encoder/decoder. C 99 scores pass despite 59 exact; 8 wrong-primer C scores also pass.
limitations: Historical source-algorithm diagnostic, not a validated autokey-family exclusion. Known-message cases reuse two passages; 247 generated truths are inadmissible under their paired decoder. Source P can skip at most primer length minus one draws; singleton P is rigid. C encoder substitutes zero for unavailable ciphertext while decoder reads the observed stream. Source gates pass on 90 runes, not the full target regime. No new global-null probability, other primers, alphabets, offsets, languages, joined pages or discarded beam-path recovery.
next_steps: A corrected common encoder/decoder model requires its own predeclared controls and target protocol; the historical algorithms and all current failures remain unchanged.
pages_note: 55 nonempty source segments map to LP2-00 through 49 and 51 through 55. LP2-50 contributes no runes to this source transcription.
bounds_note: 45 starting keys, two feedback sources and both signs; 9,900 full-page decodes, beam 450, up to 3 conditional skips per step.

scope.representation: Pinned GP29 indices,55 source segments/12,956 runes; page-local forward order. P key is primer plus that hypothesis recovered plaintext; C key is primer plus complete observed ciphertext, padded with zeros as source. Exact transcription remains external.
scope.procedure: Execute run_full_new.run_autokey semantics with unchanged P/C decoder rules. Stable cumulative-score beam returns first winner; gate its source normalized English score. Separately find first normalized maximum among retained terminal hypotheses, without changing the returned source output. Preserve all cases and control failures.
scope.parameters: 29 singleton indices plus 16 literal source words =45 distinct primers; P/C models x signs -1/+1 x 55 segments =9,900 full calls. Beam 450/max_skip 3/strict score > -5.5; no target short screen or Atbash. P frontier total skips <= primer length-1, so 3,190 singleton-P labels are rigid. Source encoder controls suppression 0.83,360 fixed seeded cases/two known readings; all outcomes retained.
scope.exclusions: Other primers/offsets/alphabets, resets inside pages, joined pages, other languages, altered encoder/frontier rules or ranking, paths discarded by the source beam and global-null significance. No general cipher-family exclusion; 247 source-generated known truths are invalid under their matching decoder.

review.kind: Complete finite historical source algorithm audit with pre-target synthetic feasibility and native parity
review.reviewer: Independent all 360 encoder/feasibility/native-control audit. Ordered synthetic parity: 228 cases/15,761 terminals. Target audit: all 19,800 saved winner paths independently scored/admissible, 3,190 singleton-P rigid equivalents; 179 native full beams enumerate 43,388 hypotheses to verify leaders/winners/normalized maxima, not all 9,900 native calls.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12, NumPy 2.5.4 and Numba 0.67.0 installed separately. Exact external transcription can be prepared from explicit local Git using prepare_input.py. Temporary replay compares all deterministic controls and target arrays, then independent native audits. No automatic installation or network.
